This development influenced many businesses to adapt and shift to online business or so -called e -commerce.

Amazon as an e -commerce platform offered hundreds of millions of products for sale s, as on June 20th, 2017 offered 372 million products online [1]. With this amount of products , amazon used the Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) as their warehouse system.

In this study, a sim ulation of the RMFS was built used NetLogo to maximize the pod utilization and minimize the energy consumption of the warehouse. This study combined 3 SKU to Pod assignments and 4 Replenishment policies.
SKU to Pod has the role to improve the pod utilizat ion by increase pick unit in each visit. Pod with more SKU types is likely to fulfill more orders.
Replenishment policy has the role to maintain the inventory of the warehouse and keep the pod at a high service level. Other than that, replenishment triggers reduced visits to the picking station.

A pod that doesn’t have sufficient capacity couldn’t be assigned with new order although it already has the most order assigned. This approach showed improvement by assigned different SKU classes in one pod and con sidering SKU inventory also with pod urgency level. Maintained the inventory level in the warehouse above 59% of total inventory influenced the warehouse performance. There was increasing of 17.83% in pod utilization and reducing of 14.75% in energy consumption. This development influenced many businesses to adapt and shift to online business or so -called e -commerce. As an example, Amazon as an e -commerce platform offered hundreds of millions of products for sales, as on June 20th, 2017 offered 372 million products online [1].

These types of products are stored in a warehouse with proper design that considering warehouse management, inventory management, and the internet of things [2]. Warehouse design has a role to maintain and improve efficiency also reduce distribution costs in the warehouse [3].

There are five main groups of warehouse systems as “picker-to-parts”, “pick-to-box”, “pick-and-sort”, “parts-to-picker”, and “completely automated picking” [4]. In parts-to-picker warehouse integrated with the Internet of Things such as data management, sensors, robot, and many other things to synchronized all processes in the warehouse.

Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) is one breakthrough in the implementation of e-commerce warehouses and is categorized as the parts-to-picker system. Kiva System as one of the innovative approaches uses hundreds of custombuilt mobile robots (AGVs) that carry small shelving units (Pods) and deliver to the assigned stations (Picking or Replenishment Station) [5]. AGVs are designed to lifting the pod, a sensing system to avoid the collision, a navigation system to help the movement of AGV , powered by battery, trolley mounted rubber wheels, and a control system as the brain of the robot [6].

Picking stations have a role to fulfill the picking order and send the products out of the warehouse. Replenishment stations have a role to maintain the product's availability in the warehouse. The combination of the picking and replenishment station is also supported by the pods' design. Pods are assigned by the types of SKUs and amount of SKUs quantity stored inside it. This policy is designed to maximize the picking and replenishment process.

SKUs dimensions, cycles, characteristics, and popularity are considered as a factor to assign SKUs to pods [7]. The SKUs need to distribute 2 in all pods with a policy such as : 1. Random, SKU assigned to the pod with random order. 2. Product similarity, integrated with order batching or order alienation to consider the product similarity by considering 2 - 40 SKUs [8] [9]. 3. Association Rules (AR), considering orders pattern as the base for correlation between the SKUs and give a combination of SKUs that can be assigned in the pod. Implement this method with a small number of SKUs ( 10 SKUs [10] and 26 SKUs [11] ) can give feasible result s, however, if a large number of SKUs being considered it showed an unfeasible combination. 4.

chunks.section: 4. Warehouse Inventory – SKU in Pod, this policy is conducted by checking the
chunks.text: However, this system ne eds to consider many factors to minimize energy consumption and maximize pod utilization. The implementation of the scenarios of SKU to Pod assignment and replenishment policy influence d the performance of the system. SKU to Pod has the role to improve the pod utilization by increase pick unit in each visit. Pod with more SKU types is likely to fulfill more orders. Replenishment policy has the role to maintain the inventory of the warehouse and keep the pod at a high service level. Other than that, replenishment triggers reduced visits to the picking station.

There are 4 scenarios in the replenishment policies as the Emptiest, Pod Inventory Level, Stockout Probability, and Warehouse Inventory – SKU in Pod.
